item.title: Molecular Chain Reaction Behind Autism Identified
item.description: Scientists identify a specific chemical process where nitric oxide disables the brain's "brakes," sending a key autism-linked growth pathway into overdrive.

item.title: Tacit Knowledge: Your Eyes Reveal the Secrets of Your Expertise
item.description: Researchers have found a way to track the "unspoken" secrets of expertise, allowing novices to master complex tasks faster than ever before.

item.title: Cocaine Addiction is a Biological Rewiring, Not a Choice
item.description: New research reveals how a single protein acts as a genetic switch, hijacking the brain's memory center to fuel cocaine addiction.

item.title: Little-Known Cells May Be Key to Clearing Alzheimer’s Proteins
item.description: New research reveals that specialized brain cells called tanycytes are responsible for clearing toxic Alzheimer’s proteins—and when they fail, the disease takes hold.

item.title: Silent Recall: Your Brain Remembers Even When You Forget
item.description: New research shows that your brain reactivates memories even when you can't recall them, suggesting a "rhythmic pulse" is the key to conscious awareness.

item.title: Chronic Inflammation Rewires the Brain’s Cognitive Center
item.description: Scientists identify the biological "signatures" that explain why some people experience brain fog and memory loss after viral infections.

item.title: Compulsivity is Driven by a Fear of the Unknown
item.description: Scientists discover that people with compulsive traits rely on repetitive behaviors because they feel less certain about how their future actions will play out.

item.title: Brain Cells Team Up as You Learn
item.description: New research reveals that as you master a skill, your brain cells stop working in isolation and start acting as a highly coordinated team.

item.title: Teen Aggression Speeds Up Aging
item.description: Aging from the inside out. Scientists find that teens who frequently lash out at others show signs of faster physical aging by the time they reach 30.

item.title: Single-Injection Immunotherapy That Halts Alzheimer’s
item.description: Scientists engineer a single-injection "cellular immunotherapy" that turns ordinary brain cells into amyloid-eating super cleaners.
